name: iCloud backup and key value store
plain: iCloud backs up the app container and offers a 1 MB key value store that survives uninstall.
meaning: Documents and Application Support are in iCloud backup unless excluded; NSUbiquitousKeyValueStore keeps up to 1 MB and 1024 keys that sync across the person's devices.

android.note: Android analog is Auto Backup and Block Store; see mob.os.auto-backup

ios.permission: iCloud entitlement for KVS and containers
ios.persistence: Backups restore app container; KVS persists across uninstall for the same Apple ID
ios.revocation: Disable iCloud for the app or delete from iCloud
ios.note: Caches and tmp excluded; Documents and Application Support included unless flagged; KVS limit 1 MB and 1024 keys (docs, from memory)

limits.headline: Can save the app's folder to iCloud and keep 1 MB of values after uninstall
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when iCloud Backup is on and the phone is charging
can: Back up documents and settings in the app's container
Keep up to 1 MB and 1024 small values, even after you delete the app
Restore the app's data on a new iPhone
cannot: Back up caches and temporary files, which are left out
Keep more than 1 MB of small values
Do this on Android, which has Auto Backup and Block Store instead
limits.reach_label: A regular copy of the app's folder
limits.differs: iPhone has iCloud Backup. Android uses Auto Backup and Block Store.

story.what_it_is: Apple's iCloud saves an app's files and a tiny note pad of settings that follow you between devices.

marketing.name: iCloud key value storage
marketing.pitch: Apple lets apps store a small set of settings that sync across a person's devices through iCloud.

story.for_you: You set up a new iPhone and your apps remember your settings. The same note pad also syncs between your iPhone and iPad.
story.for_makers: Makers get free sync of small settings and easy restores. It can also keep an old identifier alive across reinstalls and devices.

use_cases.example: A notes app syncs your theme and last note between iPhone and iPad.
A game stores your level on iCloud so a new phone picks up where you were.
A fitness app keeps your goals on all your devices.
A reader app remembers where you stopped across devices.
A team sees a stable ID that stays after a reinstall.
An ad SDK may store a device ID in the cloud to link installs.
A shopping app keeps your cart sync across devices.

story.android_note: Android uses Auto Backup and Block Store instead.
story.ios_note: Documents and Application Support are backed up unless the app excludes them. The note pad holds up to 1 MB.

history.change: iCloud and key value store introduced
